text_to_speech: at the time it was simply cataloged as a nebula or faint fuzzy patch it wouldn't be until the work of Edwin Hubble in the 1920s that many such faint fuzzy objects were understood to be self-contained galaxies of stars outside the Milky Way and Incredibly distant from us m81 is a bit too dim to see with the uned eye but it's visible with binoculars or a small telescope where it appears as a dim patch of light with a 6-in telescope you can resolve the Galaxy's bright core and with an 8-in telescope you can begin to make out the spiral arms
